issues.detail: Skill references automated tools (axe-core, Lighthouse, pa11y) but provides no concrete procedures for invoking them or interpreting their output formats.
Code examples and fixes use React/JSX syntax (htmlFor, className, JSX handlers); skill claims framework-agnostic but provides no Vue, Svelte, or vanilla JS demonstrations.

scenarios.name: form-validation-audit
scenarios.rationale: Both responses cover label associations, error message linking, and color-only error indication well. Response B explicitly addresses autocomplete attributes on standard fields (name, email)—a rubric requirement Response A entirely omits. Response B also adds WCAG standard citations and specific contrast ratio guidance, providing more comprehensive coverage of the rubric's four explicit requirements.

scenarios.name: modal-keyboard-accessibility
scenarios.rationale: Both appropriately request code first and cover Escape handling + Tab cycling + focus restoration, but Response B is more comprehensive (5 checks vs 4, includes WCAG references and promises exact fixes); both omit explicit mention of verifying visible focus indicators on all interactive elements, which the rubric requires.

scenarios.name: contrast-and-pointer-targets
scenarios.rationale: Response A provides accurate contrast calculation (7.46:1, verified against WCAG formula), correctly cites WCAG 2.5.8 for the 24×24px minimum, and offers four specific remediation approaches; Response B miscalculates contrast as ~5.3:1 (should be ~7.46:1), incorrectly attributes a 44×44 requirement to WCAG 2.1 AA (which has no explicit target-size rule at AA level), and confuses standard versions, though practical fix recommendations remain partially sound.
